On 23 July 2012 17:28, senne <jon...@gmail.com> wrote:
I'm reading the excellent book and thank Mr Williams for the efforts. I have a question about confusion matrix, in page 251:' model predict yes and observation was no for 26 observations', but on page 253 ' better than 26 days out of 41 days on which we'll end up wet', if 251 is true , that means 26 is false positive, aka no rain actually, how come in 253 we're wet? am I confused by this confusion matrix? thanks

Thanks for pointing out the typo. On page 251 the sentences before the one you quote are correct, and then the one you identify is incorrect. It should have the 'Yes' and 'No' swapped, to read: "That is, the model predicts No and the observation was Yes for 26 observations." That is, there are 26 false negatives (rather than false positives).

Regards,
Graham
